messages:
emily-support: Hey team, BrightTile reporting a sudden spike in declines for EU checkout. Several txns returning AVS mismatch + CVV fail. Sample IDs: ch_1JqXx2, ch_1JqYy3. Any quick thoughts? :eyes:
raj-payments: thanks, pulling logs now. do we have the exact billing addresses they submitted? country codes?
marta-merchant-success: sending one example from merchant DM — customer is in NL, billing_address: "Jansweg 12, 1012 AB, Amsterdam". card country: NL. They said it started after a recent address normalization change we pushed.
raj-payments: ok running a repro against gateway. I see gateway response: 
```
{"status":"declined","decline_code":"avs_mismatch","avs_result":"Z","cvv_result":"N","issuer_response_code":"A3","processor":"AcquirerX"}
```
raj-payments: AVS code Z => postal match only, address no. cvv N => cvv failed. issuer A3 typically shows address mismatch from issuer.
isaac-engineer: fwiw AVS support varies by issuer/country. in EU many issuers only check postal code; some return address mismatch if street formatting differs (accents, punctuation). What did the normalization change do?
marta-merchant-success: we stripped diacritics and collapsed punctuation to reduce duplicates. Example: "Jansweg 12B" -> "jansweg 12 b". Merchant says cardholder typed "12 B" with uppercase.
raj-payments: that could flip AVS. Repro steps I used: 1) hit our charge endpoint with original billing_address vs normalized address 2) compare gateway payload and response. Example curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/charges -d '{"amount":4900,"currency":"eur","billing":{"line1":"Jansweg 12 B","postal_code":"1012 AB","country":"NL"},"card":{"number":"4242424242424242","exp_month":12,"exp_year":2026,"cvc":"123"}}'
```
isaac-engineer: when we send normalized line1 without space/with lowercase sometimes gateway forwards exactly and issuer's AVS engine treats it as mismatch. Also note some Netherlands issuers ignore street but expect exact postal/house number format (e.g., space between number and letter).
chris-acquiring: from acquirer side, we can request more detailed AVS mapping, but issuer ultimately decides. I recommend: 1) revert aggressive normalization for street number/alpha suffix, 2) pass both raw and normalized address fields if gateway supports it (raw_for_merchant, normalized_for_search), 3) ask merchant to enable 3DS for these transactions to reduce friction.
marta-merchant-success: merchant prefers not to revert yet. Any short-term mitigations?
raj-payments: short-term: 1) allow postal_code-only AVS check for EU flows (we already do by default) but mark transactions with address mismatch for manual review; 2) reattempt with cardholder-provided CVV prompt — many declines are intermittent CVV fails too. 3) add fallback route to alternative acquirer (AcquirerY) for <5% traffic to see if declines reduce.
emily-support: merchant asks if this could be a fraud engine false positive combined with AVS.
isaac-engineer: yes risk engines often weight AVS+CVV. Our charge payload currently sets risk.metadata.address_normalized=true; that might bump score. We can temporarily suppress that flag for this merchant to avoid auto-declines.
chris-acquiring: I'm opening escalation with AcquirerX — will ask for issuer AVS detail and whether they expect a specific house number format. created ticket ACQ-9876.
payments-bot: Created internal ticket PAY-4321 to track merchant BrightTile AVS/CVV escalation and normalization rollback request. Follow-up sync scheduled: 2024-11-06 14:00 UTC.
emily-support: thanks — I'll relay: revert street normalization for now, enable 3DS, try small reattempts and we wait on ACQ-9876. :thumbsup:
marta-merchant-success: merchant will try revert tonight and run a small retry batch in the morning. will update here.
chris-acquiring: quick note — for EU corporate cards, AVS is unreliable; if declines persist after revert we should consider processing as card-not-present but with enhanced dispute protections (MCC/TID flags) when merchant provides PoC of delivery.
raj-payments: closing loop: reproduced locally, change in normalization was root cause in ~70% repro cases. marking as actionable.
emily-support: great, moving to resolved once merchant confirms reattempt results.
payments-bot: UPDATE: merchant reattempt batch 11/04 07:24 UTC -> decline rate dropped from 12% -> 2.1%. keeping ticket open until 11/08 for final sign-off. :white_check_mark:
